creativePrompt: Use only the supplied Tears of Steel source video to make a 12-second widescreen action edit called Velocity. Inspect the source first and choose four genuinely energetic shots with clear camera or subject motion; avoid dialogue-only holds and credits. Build a readable arc: 0–2s an intriguing moving detail, 2–5s three escalating action cuts, 5–8s one hero movement that eases from 100% to 45% speed for its peak then accelerates to 220%, 8–11s a decisive payoff, 11–12s a clean visual finish. Cut on matching movement directions and use two 6-frame whip transitions only where source motion supports them. Add a single 6% punch-in on the strongest impact. Preserve sharp faces and edges; use frame sampling if interpolation bends objects. Keep original environmental sound where useful, add a restrained original percussive pulse and two synchronized impacts, and duck the pulse under any retained intelligible speech. No stock footage, no new generated scenes, no full-screen captions, and no random flash/glitch effects. Deliver one polished 1920x1080 H264 MP4 with intentional crops, no stretched image, plus source timecodes and an edit decision list. The edit must still clearly communicate acceleration and payoff when muted.
